items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: when Papa Celestine first came here, and we played with the, uh, uh, Tuxedo Band, which he still kept that name, Tuxedo Band.

ctx.x: Yes, you can always copyright your own arrangement, of course.

Well, that's what I did. I got my own arrangement copyrighted, you see. And, oh, it went on nice, it went on nice. We should sing that. Yeah. And I was fixing to get the boys together, because I, very few musicians I know now, they all, you're all my old musician friends, they're all gone. I suppose. Yeah, I remember, and Peter Brokaw, and about some of the only ones that I can remember back that time, you understand? I, I, I don't know of any other of the old musicians. Of course, that was Papa Celestine, but I…
And, uh, I was gonna ask, when did you start to work for the post office? I started to work for the post office in 1906.
